answer:

The peritoneum is a continuous serous membrane that lines the abdominal cavity. It consists of two main parts:

1.  **Parietal Peritoneum:** This layer lines the interior wall of the abdominal cavity. It is present along the inner edges of the reflected abdominal wall seen in the image.
2.  **Visceral Peritoneum:** This layer covers the abdominal organs. The smooth outer surfaces of the intestinal loops visible in the center of the image are covered by the visceral peritoneum.

Because it is a very thin, transparent membrane, it may not appear as a distinct, thick layer of tissue, but it is an integral anatomical structure that remains present in this dissection.

original.answer:
Based on the image provided, the peritoneum **is present**.

The peritoneum is a serous membrane that lines the abdominal cavity (parietal peritoneum) and covers the abdominal organs (visceral peritoneum).

In this autopsy image, you can see the glistening, smooth, semi-transparent layer covering the loops of the intestines; this is the **visceral peritoneum**.

While the abdominal wall has been opened to expose the organs (meaning the peritoneal cavity is now open to the air), the membrane itself remains present on the surfaces of the organs and the inner lining of the body wall.
